feedback: If the learner says a coast is always sandy, show a rocky shore and a muddy estuary beside a sandy beach: all three are coasts; define coast by land-meets-sea, then re-sort the types.
If they describe a coast as a holiday resort, trace the whole coastline on a map — most of it has no holiday-makers; it is a boundary, not a destination.
If they say every coast has the same animals, pair each type with a typical resident (rocky → limpet/crab; sandy → burrowing worm/cockle; muddy → wading bird) and ask them to match again.
activities.intendedInsight: A coast is defined by the land–sea boundary (including cliffs and mudflats), not by sand or by being a holiday spot, and its type shapes which animals live there.
learnerActions: Answer in your own words: 'What is a coast?' — aiming for 'where land meets the ocean', not 'a sandy beach'.
Name at least two kinds of coast (sandy, rocky, muddy).
Name one animal you would expect at each kind of coast you named.
Decide whether a rocky cliff with waves at its base is a coast, and explain why.
Trace the edge where land meets the sea on a map all the way round and say whether the whole line is coast, even the parts with no people.
activities.title: Say what a coast really is

feedback: Affirm and extend a memory: 'You found a shell on the sand — lots of shelled animals bury into soft sand like that.'
Gently redirect a vague answer toward the shore material and its life: 'Was it rocky or muddy where you saw the crab? What do crabs like about the rocks?'
activities.intendedInsight: New coast vocabulary connects to the learner's own remembered experiences, and even a familiar beach trip can be sorted into shore types with their typical life.
learnerActions: Talk with a 'beach ranger' (an adult, puppet, or role-play voice) about what you have found or might find at the beach.
Describe something you saw and say which shore it came from — sand, rock, or mud.
Answer the ranger's follow-ups: 'What was the ground like there?' and 'What animal did you see, and why was it there?'
activities.title: Tell the ranger about your beach day
